Footers read ( 9 - A ), ( 11 - A ), ( 13 - A ); TFDD-B-AGT at foot left on all three. Series A confirmed on every page. p11's footer is badly defocused -- the page digits are unreadable as glyphs, but the series glyph is an unmistakable triangle-with-crossbar (A), not a D bowl.

BAND IS Q51-66, SIXTEEN questions -- NOT Q51-67 as the dispatch estimated. p9 = Q51-55, p11 = Q56-60, p13 = Q61-66. PART - B is headed on printed 9 and Q51 is its first question.

SEAMS: BOTH CLEAN, no question straddles either boundary. p7 (before) ends with Q50 complete, all four options printed -- Part A closes on that page. p15 (after) opens with Q67 at the top of its left column, and Q66 on p13 is complete with all four options. b5 owns Q67 onward.

FIGURES: NONE. No diagram anywhere on the three pages; every question is fully stated in words. Consistent with the brief's measured finding that this paper has none.

SET D CROSS-READ (see the per-question flags on Q58 and Q60): printed pages 11 and 13 of Set A are photographed far worse than p9, and the Q58 and Q60 option blocks are backed by only ~109x73 and ~85x24 REAL source pixels, so no zoom adds information. Per config.ts ('Set D is the place to re-read any Set A region that is defocused near the binding ... ONLY after a question has been matched on independently legible content'), Set D was consulted. Every one of my sixteen questions has a legible Set A stem, so all sixteen were matched on independently legible content before any Set D option was read, and Set D was used to supply a CANDIDATE SET only -- each Set A label was then re-checked against its own glyphs. Note FIDELITY_BRIEF.md is referenced by config.ts but does not exist in scripts/nda-gat yet.

EVIDENCE THAT THE TWO SERIES SHARE OPTION ORDER, for whoever builds the variant map: all sixteen of my questions appear in Set D and NOT ONE has its options permuted. Set A Q51-55 = Set D Q91-95, Q56-60 = Set D Q96-100, Q61-66 = Set D Q76-81, label for label. This is corroboration, not an assumption I relied on: Q51-57, Q59 and Q61-66 were read off Set A first and Set D agreed afterwards.

AND THE SET D OFFSET IS NOT CONSTANT -- do not assume one. Within this Physics block it is +40 for Set A Q51-60 and +15 for Set A Q61-66 (and Set A Q67-70 = Set D Q82-85, also +15). Set D leads with Set A's Q61-75 and then takes Q51-60, i.e. a rotation WITHIN the block, not a shift. Set D's Part B also opens on a different subject entirely (Biology, not Physics).

questions.stem: Which of the following is correct regarding the total internal reflection at the interface between two different optical media ?

options.label: A
options.text: The phenomenon of total internal reflection can occur only if light is passing at any angle from a medium of low refractive index to a medium of high refractive index.

options.label: B
options.text: The phenomenon of total internal reflection can occur only if light is passing from a medium of high refractive index to a medium of low refractive index and at an angle greater than the critical angle.

options.label: C
options.text: The phenomenon of total internal reflection can occur only if light is passing at any angle from a medium of high refractive index to a medium of low refractive index.

options.label: D
options.text: The phenomenon of total internal reflection can occur only if light is passing from a medium of low refractive index to a medium of high refractive index and at an angle greater than the critical angle.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements :
I. The weight of an object is the same everywhere on the surface of the Earth, but its inertial mass could be different.
II. The inertial mass and gravitational mass of an object are proportional and the proportionality constant is the same everywhere.
III. The inertial mass and weight of an object are the same at different places on Earth.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.subject: Physics
flags: Taxonomy: closest fit. The question is about inertial vs gravitational mass and the variation of weight over the Earth's surface; the Gravitation chapter has no 'mass and weight' subtopic, so it is filed under Newton's Law of Gravitation (where gravitational mass lives). Gravitational Field and Potential is the rival fit.

questions.stem:
Consider the following :
I. Gravitational field due to a spherical body
II. Electrostatic field due to a point charge
III. Strong nuclear force field due to a proton
IV. Magnetic field due to a bar magnet
How many of the above follow the inverse square law ?
questions.subject: Physics
flags: Taxonomy: FORCED FIT. The question spans four different force fields (gravitational, electrostatic, strong nuclear, magnetic) and its actual subject is the inverse-square law itself, which no chapter owns. Filed under Gravitation / Newton's Law of Gravitation as the canonical home of the inverse-square law. Electricity and Magnetism / Electrostatics is an equally defensible rival.

questions.stem: A particle of mass \(m\) moves along x-direction under the force \(F(x) = F_0\left(1 - \frac{x}{L}\right)\) for \(0 \le x \le L\). If the particle starts from rest at \(x = 0\), then what is the speed \((v)\) of the particle at \(x = L\) ?
questions.subject: Physics
flags: Read off Set A at high zoom: A's numerator is one glyph WIDER than B's and C's (the leading 2), and C's denominator is one glyph wider than A's and B's (the leading 2 of 2m). That mutual contrast is the discriminator and it is internally consistent. Independently confirmed against Set D Q99, same four options in the same label order.

flags: WORST-LEGIBILITY BLOCK IN THE BAND. Faded ink + defocus + the red watermark. On Set A's own page I can establish: A and B each carry a radical with a FOUR-glyph numerator over a single-glyph denominator consistent with 3; C and D carry NO radical; and C's value is a wide two-lobed glyph (infinity), not a round 0. D's value is completely obscured by the watermark and is NOT independently visible on Set A -- it is the remaining member of a four-option set whose other three are placed, and Set D Q100 confirms it as 0. The 4 vs 2 in the A/B numerators is likewise below Set A's resolution and comes from Set D. See the band report for the Set A/Set D label-order evidence.
